dialogue.content: こんにちは
dialogue.English: Hello.

dialogue.content: こんにちは今日はよろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Hello. It's nice to meet you today.

dialogue.content: お願い致します
dialogue.English: You too.

dialogue.content: 0時になったらお声掛けしますね、もしくは可能であれば、さっそく始めますか？
dialogue.English: I can call on you at the scheduled time, or if you're ready, shall we begin now?

dialogue.content: はい、大丈夫です
dialogue.English: Yes, that's fine.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございますでは、始めましょうよろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Thank you. Then, let's begin. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: 宜しくお願いします
dialogue.English: Me too.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。ご相談ありがとうございます。まず初めに、年齢と性別と、何とおよびしたらよいか、教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Hello. Thank you for reaching out. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you would like me to call you?

dialogue.content: こんにちはまりです14才、女性です
dialogue.English: Hello, I’m Mari, 14 years old, female.

dialogue.content: まりさん、よろしくお願いします。では、今日はどんなお話をしましょうか
dialogue.English: It's nice to meet you, Mari. So, what would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 友達とうまくいかなくて
dialogue.English: I’m not getting along with a friend.

dialogue.content: って言うかうざい
dialogue.English: Or rather, she’s really annoying.

dialogue.content: そうですか。。。それはつらいですね
dialogue.English: I see... That must be difficult.

dialogue.content: イラっときます
dialogue.English: It's so irritating.

dialogue.content: うざい状況、もっと詳しくおしえてください
dialogue.English: Could you tell me more about this annoying situation?

dialogue.content: いつもすっごい話かけて来るし、違う場所にいても探して来る
dialogue.English: She's always talking to me, and even if I'm in a different place, she'll come looking for me.

dialogue.content: ええ！そうなんですね。まるでストーカーのように感じてしまいますね
dialogue.English: Oh wow, I see. That must feel almost like being stalked.

dialogue.content: そうです
dialogue.English: Yes, it does.

dialogue.content: それは、同じクラスの友達ですか？
dialogue.English: Is she a classmate?

dialogue.content: 男？女？
dialogue.English: A boy? A girl?

dialogue.content: 中学入ってからずっと一緒にお弁当食べる女子です
dialogue.English: She's a girl I've been eating lunch with ever since we started middle school.

dialogue.content: 中学入ってからとなると、2年くらいずーっと我慢していたのかな？
dialogue.English: Since the start of middle school... does that mean you've been putting up with this for about two years?

dialogue.content: 最初は私も話して楽しかったんだけど、2年になってから私の話は聞いてくれないのに、相手ばっかり話して来ます
dialogue.English: At first, I enjoyed talking with her too, but since our second year, she doesn't listen to what I have to say and just talks about herself.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。人の話は聞かないけど、自分の話ばかりしてくるのね。。それはうざいね
dialogue.English: I see. So she doesn't listen to you, but only talks about herself... That does sound annoying.

dialogue.content: うん
dialogue.English: Yeah.

dialogue.content: どんなこと話してくるのかしら？
dialogue.English: What kinds of things does she talk about?

dialogue.content: 愚痴
dialogue.English: Complaints.

dialogue.content: 愚痴は聞いているほうも心がすさんでくるよね
dialogue.English: Listening to complaints can be really draining, can't it?

dialogue.content: あと、ぜんぜん言うこと聞いてくれない
dialogue.English: Also, she doesn't listen to a thing I say.

dialogue.content: いうこと聞かないの？？？？よく耐えているね！
dialogue.English: She doesn't listen at all? You've been very patient!

dialogue.content: ずっと一緒にいるし、追っかけてくるから
dialogue.English: Because we're always together and she follows me around.

dialogue.content: 仕方ないし
dialogue.English: I have no choice.

dialogue.content: そうなのね！！！！苦しいね…ほかに、一緒にお弁当食べている友達はいないのかな？
dialogue.English: I see! That must be tough... Are there any other friends you eat lunch with?

dialogue.content: たまに別の子も仲良い子が休んだりして混ざるけど、ほとんど二人
dialogue.English: Sometimes another friend joins if their own close friend is absent, but it's usually just the two of us.

dialogue.content: そっか・・それは逃げ道がないね。。。優しいまりさんのこと好きで仕方ないんだね
dialogue.English: I see... so there's no way to escape. She must really like you for being so kind, Mari.

dialogue.content: そうかもだけど、自分の愚痴ばっかりだから
dialogue.English: Maybe, but it's just all her own complaints.

dialogue.content: 疲れる
dialogue.English: It’s exhausting.

dialogue.content: 愚痴ばかり聞いていると、へとへとになってしまうよね。。。まりさんの体調が心配になってしまいます
dialogue.English: Listening to nothing but complaints would make anyone exhausted... I'm worried about your well-being.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 学校行きたくないです
dialogue.English: I don’t want to go to school.

dialogue.content: そのうざいお友達は、何に満足しなくて愚痴ばかり言うのかしら
dialogue.English: I wonder what your friend is dissatisfied with that makes her complain all the time.

dialogue.content: 親とか先生とか友達の事もなんか気に入らないとすが言って来る
dialogue.English: She'll complain about her parents, teachers, and friends as soon as something displeases her.

dialogue.content: そのうざいお友達はすべての人間に対して不満を持っているのね。。。
dialogue.English: It sounds like she has complaints about everyone.

dialogue.content: 不満でいっぱいで、愚痴ばかり言う人は、実は自分に自信がない人が多いんですよね
dialogue.English: You know, people who are full of complaints and always grumbling often actually lack self-confidence.

dialogue.content: えー
dialogue.English: Really?

dialogue.content: 自信満々ですよ
dialogue.English: She seems completely confident.

dialogue.content: いつも上から出し
dialogue.English: She’s always talking down to people.

dialogue.content: 出し
dialogue.English: Talking down.

dialogue.content: マウンティングっていう言葉、聞いたことあるかな？自信のない自分を隠そうとして、無意識にわざわざ人をけなして自分のほうが有利だって自分に言い聞かせているの。
dialogue.English: Have you heard the term “mounting” (social one-upmanship)? In trying to hide their own insecurity, some people unconsciously put others down to convince themselves they’re in a superior position.

dialogue.content: マウンティング？
dialogue.English: “Mounting”?

dialogue.content: わからないです
dialogue.English: I don't know what that is.

dialogue.content: あーでも、そういう感じです
dialogue.English: Ah, but that’s what it feels like.

dialogue.content: ごめんね！マウンティングっているのは、人より有利になって優越感を感じることだよ
dialogue.English: Sorry for the jargon. “Mounting” means trying to be in a superior position to feel a sense of superiority.

dialogue.content: そんなこといいじゃん、ってことにブーブー言ってる
dialogue.English: She grumbles and complains about things that I think don't even matter.

dialogue.content: で、まりもそう思うでしょって
dialogue.English: And then she says, "You think so too, right Mari?"

dialogue.content: でも、本当に自信があって、優しい人は、そんな上からものを言ったりするかな？少なくとも、優しいまりさんはそんなことしないでしょ？
dialogue.English: But would someone who is truly confident and kind talk down to others like that? At least, a kind person like you wouldn't do that, would you, Mari?

dialogue.content: そう思うでしょ？って言われたら「うん」って言わざるを得ないよね。。。そんな時はどう対処しているの？
dialogue.English: When she asks, "You think so too, right?" you must feel like you have to say "yes"... How do you usually handle that?

dialogue.content: 私は悪口言いたくないし、そんなことどうでもいいじゃんって思うから「へー」とか「そーなんだー」とか、フワッとしてるんです
dialogue.English: I don’t want to badmouth people, and I feel like those things don’t matter, so I stay vague like, “Oh, really,” or “I see.”

dialogue.content: だから疲れちゃって、学校行くのすごいめんどい
dialogue.English: So I get worn out, and going to school feels like such a hassle.

dialogue.content: すごい！！！！あたりさわりない返事、大人でも難しいことをまりさん日ごろからやっているんだね！！・・・けど、ずいぶん疲れ切ってしまっているね
dialogue.English: That's amazing! Giving non-committal answers is something even adults find difficult, and you're doing it all the time, Mari! ...But it sounds like you're completely worn out.

dialogue.content: うん
dialogue.English: Yeah.

dialogue.content: そんなんなら学校行きたくないね
dialogue.English: No wonder you don’t want to go to school.

dialogue.content: 大人じゃないけど
dialogue.English: I’m not an adult, though.

dialogue.content: 前、そのことで先生にまりもそう言ってるって聞いたって言われたから
dialogue.English: Because before, a teacher told me that they heard from my friend that I was saying those things too.

dialogue.content: えええええ！！！うざいお友達は、まりさんを仲間にしようとたくらんでいるのかな
dialogue.English: What?! It sounds like your annoying friend is trying to make you her accomplice.

dialogue.content: さて、どうしたらいいものか。。。
dialogue.English: Now then, what would be the best way to handle this...

dialogue.content: 仲間っていうか、自分の話とおんなじって思いたい見たいな
dialogue.English: Not so much an ally, more like she wants to believe I feel the same way she does.

dialogue.content: ほら、自信ないからまりさんが同意してくれることで自信を保とうとしているでしょ？自分の中で、どんなふうになったら楽しい学校生活取り戻せそう？？？
dialogue.English: See? She's not confident, so she's trying to maintain her confidence by getting you to agree with her, right? In your mind, what would need to happen for you to get your enjoyable school life back?

dialogue.content: っていうイメージはあるかな？
dialogue.English: Do you have that kind of picture in mind?

dialogue.content: うーん、離れたいかな
dialogue.English: Hmm, I think I want some distance.

dialogue.content: めんどいから学校行きたくない
dialogue.English: It’s such a hassle that I don’t want to go to school.

dialogue.content: そうだね。私もそのうざいお友達と離れることが一番だと思う。うざいお友達のせいでせっかくの楽しい学校生活台無しにされたくないよね
dialogue.English: I agree. I also think distancing yourself from this annoying friend is the best course of action. You don't want her to ruin your otherwise enjoyable school life, right?

dialogue.content: でも、離れることはできそうかな？・・・難しいよね
dialogue.English: But does it seem possible to create that distance? It’s hard, isn’t it?

dialogue.content: 逆恨みされてもこわいよね
dialogue.English: And it would be scary if she held a grudge.

dialogue.content: でも一人もやだから
dialogue.English: But I don't want to be alone either.

dialogue.content: 学校行かないのが楽
dialogue.English: Not going to school would be easier.

dialogue.content: 同じクラスに頼れそうなお友達は他にいないかな？「実はこんなことになってて、、、助けてほしいの」って相談できるお友達！
dialogue.English: Is there anyone else in your class you could rely on? A friend you could say, "This is what’s been happening... I need help," to?

dialogue.content: 前、言ったんだけど「そーいうこだよねー」って流された
dialogue.English: I tried saying something before, but they brushed it off with, "Yeah, that’s how she is."

dialogue.content: そうなんだね！ほかの子も同じこと思っているんだね！思い切って「助けて！」って言ってみたかな？
dialogue.English: I see—so others think the same. Have you tried taking the plunge and saying, "Please help me"?

dialogue.content: でも、さっきの逆恨み？みたいになるから言えない・・・
dialogue.English: But I can’t, because I’m afraid she’d hold a grudge like you mentioned...

dialogue.content: けど、ひとりで抱えていたら、本当に具合悪くなっちゃうんじゃないかって心配よ少なくとも、お弁当の時間、みんなの輪に混ぜてもらうとか。。とりあえずうざいお友達も。
dialogue.English: But I'm worried that if you keep holding this in all by yourself, you'll really get sick. At the very least, maybe you could try joining a group of friends for lunch... and just bring the annoying friend along for now.

dialogue.content: うざいお友達を仲間はずれにするんじゃなくて、まりさんの役割をみんなでできればいいのだけれど。。。
dialogue.English: Rather than excluding her, it would be good if everyone could share the role that you’ve been carrying.

dialogue.content: なんて言えばいいかわからない、友達は私が他の子と仲良くするとすごく突っ込んで聞いてくるから
dialogue.English: I don't know what to say. When I get friendly with other kids, she interrogates me about it.

dialogue.content: そっか。。。それはおびえてしまうよね。。先生は頼りになりそうな感じ？
dialogue.English: I see... that can be intimidating. Do you think a teacher might be someone you can rely on?

dialogue.content: 頼りになるけど先生に言ったのが友達にバレたら・・・
dialogue.English: They are reliable, but if my friend finds out I told a teacher...

dialogue.content: 頼りになる先生で良かった！！なんだかいつもそのうざいお友達に見張られているような恐怖心を持ってしまっているね。。先生は守秘義務って聞いたことある？「秘密は守ります」っていう義務が先生にはあるのよ
dialogue.English: It's good you have a teacher you can rely on! It sounds like you're living in fear of being watched by this friend all the time. Have you heard of confidentiality? Teachers have a duty to "keep your secrets."

dialogue.content: そうなんエア・・・
dialogue.English: Is that so...?

dialogue.content: だ
dialogue.English: Yeah.

dialogue.content: そうなの！どう？まずは先生に相談できそう？
dialogue.English: That’s right. How do you feel—could you start by talking with a teacher?

dialogue.content: 私は、まず第一にまりさん一人で背負っている苦しみから解放されてほしいの！
dialogue.English: First and foremost, I want you to be freed from carrying this burden alone.

dialogue.content: 友達がくっついてくるから、一人で行ける時がなさそう
dialogue.English: My friend is always stuck to me, so there's probably no time I can go alone.

dialogue.content: わーーー。。いつもぴったりくっついてくるんだ。本当によく耐えているよね！！
dialogue.English: Wow... she’s always right next to you. You’ve really been enduring a lot.

dialogue.content: 先生に手紙書いたらどうだろうか
dialogue.English: How about writing a letter to the teacher?

dialogue.content: そっか
dialogue.English: Oh, right.

dialogue.content: それならできそう
dialogue.English: I think I could do that.

dialogue.content: できそうかな？それで、こっそり先生と話しできる方法を先生は考えてくれると思うよ！
dialogue.English: Does that feel doable? I think the teacher will then come up with a way for you two to talk privately.

dialogue.content: できそうです！
dialogue.English: I can do that!

dialogue.content: ありがとう
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: まず、先生につらいことを話して自分だけの苦しみを先生と半分こしてみよう！あ、私もいるから、三分の一個だね！！
dialogue.English: First, let's try telling the teacher about what's been so hard and share that burden with them! Oh, and I'm here too, so we can split it three ways!

dialogue.content: それから次の手段を考えてみようか！
dialogue.English: Then we can think about the next steps.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: そうします
dialogue.English: I’ll do that.

dialogue.content: まりさん、本当に怖い思いをずっと耐えてきたね。。。お話聞いてて涙が出そうになった。話してくれて、本当にありがとう！！
dialogue.English: Mari, you've been enduring such a scary situation for so long... Listening to your story almost brought me to tears. Thank you so much for telling me!

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 人に話すの初めてだったから、ちょっと怖かったけど話してよかったです
dialogue.English: This was the first time I've talked to anyone about this, so I was a little scared, but I'm glad I did.

dialogue.content: また、怖かったり、辛かったり、疲れてしまった時に、お話しにきてね！まりさんのつらい気持ち、私と半分こしようね！！
dialogue.English: Please come and talk to me again anytime you feel scared, sad, or tired! Let's share your difficult feelings, okay?

dialogue.content: はい！また相談します
dialogue.English: Okay! I'll come back for advice again.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: ありがとう！！あと、何か言い忘れたこととかあるかな？
dialogue.English: Thank you! Is there anything else you forgot to mention?

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です
dialogue.English: I'm fine.

dialogue.content: そっか！それじゃあ、今日はいったんここまでにしましょう。ゆっくり休んでね！！ありがとうございました！
dialogue.English: I see! Well then, let's end our session here for today. Please get some rest! Thank you very much!

dialogue.content: （実はこの相談は私が受けて、うまく共感できなかったものを真似てみたものです。本当に勉強になりました。）
dialogue.English: (Actually, this consultation is based on one I handled where I couldn't empathize well, so I tried imitating it. It was really educational.)

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much.)

dialogue.content: （そうだったんですね。。私も手に汗握りながら14歳まりさんの気持ちに近づこうと頑張ってみました。これからもたくさんの壁にお互いぶつかると思いますが、ともに頑張りましょうね！！！！！！！！）
dialogue.English: (Oh, I see... I was on the edge of my seat trying my best to get close to the feelings of a 14-year-old Mari. I'm sure we'll both run into many walls from now on, but let's do our best together!)

dialogue.content: (今日は本当にありがとうございました。では、ロールプレイを終了しますね！またお会いできる日までどうぞお元気で！)
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much for today. Let’s end the role-play here. Until we meet again, please take care!)

dialogue.content: （「まりさんにちかづく」ですね。どうしても大人目線で話してしまっていたので頑張ってトレーニングします！ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (“Getting closer to Mari,” right? I kept ending up speaking from an adult’s perspective, so I’ll work hard on training. Thank you.)

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、手探りですが、頑張ります！ありがとうございました！！では終了してもよろしいですか？
dialogue.English: Likewise—I’m still feeling my way through, but I’ll do my best. Thank you! Is it okay to end here?
